claim: Preschoolers (about 4 years) infer causal structure from covariation, screening-off and interventions in small deterministic systems of 2-3 variables, well above chance (e.g. 64% correct on both trials vs 6-33% in controls, n=25 vs 18 each).
agent_test: Give agent small hidden-cause puzzles; compare REVISE with and without explicit causal-graph state at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The Bayesian reading is contested: a domain-general associative network (McClelland & Thompson 2007) fits the same group data, and 4-year-old answers lie inside a probability-matching interval. Children's rates (67% object called blicket 16%/78%) are noisier than the normative model.
agent_test: No agent test needed; treat 'Bayesian' as a design metaphor, not evidence for any specific mechanism.

claim: Backward blocking is not robust outside the original child task: six-month-olds (n=19, F(3,54)=0.28 p=.84) and adults (n=60, rating of B did not drop significantly) fail to show it in Benton & Rakison. Later checks: three-year-olds show no backward blocking (Beckers 2009, abstract only); adults show it in an incidental reaction-time task (PLoS One 2024) but not in a rating task. No LLM backward-blocking study was found.
agent_test: Do not assume retroactive discounting; test whether agent re-scores earlier evidence when a later one explains it away.

claim: Children are not reliably better scientists with more uncertain causes: with 4 candidate causes, 4-7 year-olds are at chance (33%) and only 8-10 year-olds beat it (p=.007 blicket, p<.001 butterfly, N=242; replicated N=112); a category-membership version stayed at 27% (N=110).
agent_test: Scale hypothesis count (2, 4, 8 causes) and measure REVISE accuracy; expect a cliff, not a smooth decline.

claim: Young children favour overhypothesis-consistent, broad hypotheses over adults: 4-year-olds call the key object a blicket under the conjunctive rule 92% vs adults 25%; the curve falls 0.56 (6-7), 0.60 (9-11), 0.28 (12-14). Numbers now checked in the PNAS paper (opened): 0.92, 0.56, 0.60, 0.28, 0.25; the 4-year-old and adult cells are reused from Lucas 2014.
agent_test: Test whether higher-temperature or broader hypothesis generation (O1) helps on unlikely-rule tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Active exploration beats passive observation for adults on conjunctive (AND) identification: active 0.69, passive observer 0.45, passive proposer 0.12 (N=306); the old child-better-than-adult result is partly a passive-design effect. The paper is now accepted at CogSci 2026. Still adults only: no child active-exploration arm.
agent_test: Compare agent choosing its own tests vs reading a fixed transcript of the same tests at equal tokens.

claim: Children given the hypothesis space explore efficiently: 71% vs 32% produce enough data to settle the rule (N=85, p=.002); about 17.5% test the empty machine.
agent_test: Give the agent an enumerated list of candidate rules vs none; measure disambiguating tests.

claim: Current LLM agents do worse on AND than OR rules and with 8 vs 4 objects; they explore at times worse than random; information gain correlates with success (Spearman 0.76). Update: gpt-5 and deepseek-reasoner are near-perfect on OR and much better on AND than older models, but still below top humans; higher o3-mini/o4-mini effort made 8-object AND exploration worse.
agent_test: Add explicit hypothesis-elimination bookkeeping; measure tests-to-solve on AND vs OR.

claim: Giving LLMs oracle (information-gain) exploration data raises accuracy but most stay below perfect, and starting with more hypotheses (16-96) removes the AND-OR gap: the bottleneck is hypothesis generation and exploration. Caveat: more unique seeds change hypothesis count and prior flatness at once, so the two causes are not separated.
agent_test: Seed S1/O1 with a large enumerated hypothesis pool before testing; compare to default at equal tokens.

claim: Counterexample-seeking prompts (Think-in-Opposites) raise falsifying tests and success in thinking models: Wason Qwen3-8B 0.21 to 0.36, 32B 0.41 to 0.61; blicket 8B 0.32 to 0.40, 32B 0.57 to 0.86; non-thinking blicket 8B 0.11 to 0.19. Effects are small or mixed in non-thinking models. The link between negative testing and success is also found by an outside lab, as a correlation (FALSIFYBENCH, rho=-0.779, 12 models).
agent_test: Add a think-in-opposites step to REVISE; measure incompatible-to-compatible test ratio and success.
note: The earlier 0.21 to 0.40 figure mixed the Wason and blicket tasks; resolved in d07. The prompt effect itself has no outside replication; tokens are not matched.

claim: LLMs match children on imitation but trail on innovation (2023 models: GPT-4 75.9% innovation, Claude 58.2% vs adults 95.7%); older RL and GPT-3/PaLM tests failed the blicket-style tasks.
agent_test: Old-model finding; re-run innovation task with current model at equal tokens before relying on it.

claim: Iterative hypothesis refinement helps on rule-induction tasks but with caveats: ACRE raw accuracy IO 64.0 to 82.5 (T=3,N=5); ARC subset 17% to 30-33% with hypothesis filtering; active online rule revision solves 0.35 of ActiveACRE vs 0.00 for direct LLM. Counter-evidence: at equal token cost nothing beat repeated sampling on math with 1.5B-7B models, and self-inspecting methods lost (Mirzaei 2026); orchestration gains over tuned CoT are at most 4.6 points at 2-4x tokens (Leins 2026). No blicket-type equal-token test exists.
agent_test: Run refine-loop vs best-of-N at equal tokens; the cited gains are not token-matched.

claim: Architecture scaffolding (context graph plus monitors) improved post-switch causal reasoning from 73.3% to 93.9-95.3% in Claude Sonnet 4.5, but raw pooled accuracy for graph alone was lower (77.3 vs 87.3%); gains are fragile and from one company-lab preprint. Boundary: with probabilistic activation (p=0.70) all agents sit at 73-77% and the scaffold adds nothing; no outside replication or cross-model run found.
agent_test: Replicate with our own schema at equal tokens; pooled accuracy, not subset, is the metric.

claim: LLMs use only about half their intervention budget and rarely check final hypotheses against data; one check lifts 4-node accuracy 48% to 60%.
agent_test: Force a final consistency check against all collected data before commit; measure.

claim: Teaching or pedagogical framing narrows child exploration (play time 119.2 vs 205.7 s baseline; actions kinds 4.00 vs 6.15). Numbers checked in the Cognition paper (opened): N=85, Exp 1 hidden functions found 0.72 pedagogical vs 1.15 baseline (F(1,81)=4.58, p<.05). A 2026 adult study found heuristics kept search broader than finished solutions (abstract only). No LLM test found.
agent_test: Compare agent with directive plan vs open exploration prompt; expect narrower search with directive.

claim: The theory-theory stage view is partly supported by mixed-strategy data: children give a mix of realist and false-belief answers; 65% passed more than 75% of tasks, about 30% passed fewer than 25% (Liu et al. 2007 via review).
agent_test: Not testable on agent directly; note that single traces may show mixed strategies.

claim: At equal token cost, methods in which a small model critiques or rewrites its own answer do not beat repeated sampling (math, Qwen2.5 1.5B-7B, 36 comparisons: 0 better, 10 worse). Nobody has run this equal-token test on blicket-type induction, so the gain of a REVISE loop over best-of-N there is unknown.
agent_test: Run REVISE with test results vs N independent runs plus a data-consistency check at equal total tokens on hidden-rule puzzles; report both.

claim: Confirmation-biased testing predicts failure in LLMs in two independent labs: Jhaveri (I:C vs success correlated in thinking and non-thinking Qwen3 models) and FALSIFYBENCH (Spearman -0.779 across 12 models; odds ratio 0.016 over the full bias range; won games 20% bias vs lost games 50% for GPT-5.2-Chat).
agent_test: Log the share of tests that lie outside the current hypothesis at S5; flag runs where it stays near zero.

claim: Probabilistic (noisy) machines remove the benefit of a context-graph plus monitor scaffold: with activation probability 0.70, Base, CG and CG+DB score 76.7%, 76.7% and 73.3% (n=30 each) although the noise monitor fired in 77% of episodes. Seeing the noise is not the same as handling it.
agent_test: Add a repeat-the-same-test and tally step for noisy tasks; compare with and without.

claim: Planning tests without seeing their outcomes is worse than watching: adult AND object identification was 0.69 active, 0.45 passive observer, 0.12 passive proposer (N=306).
agent_test: Compare an agent that writes all tests up front with one that sees each result before choosing the next.

claim: No outside lab has replicated the context-graph scaffold (Alderete) or the counterexample-prompt intervention (Jhaveri) on another model family or task; the blicket-LLM papers share authors (GX-Chen, Samiei, Gopnik).
agent_test: Repeat both on the schema's own model at equal tokens before counting either as supported.
